text.text_excerpt: wanted to come here for a long long time. I was a little surprized that the menu was so "creole/cajun". I knew that it was, but thought there might be a little more variety to it. however, it was wonderful. we had the sampler plate of appetizers. lots of food to share, and then we split a nice poboy, with chicken, ham, and blue cheese. light, tasty, and filling. it was an early afternoon, and blazing hot outside, and NO ONE was there. we had the waiter to ourselves, and he was there at every turn. normally? I don't care for "bourbon street" food, but these folks aren't priced like bourbon, NOR are they serving up plates of greasy junk food. everything was perfect. I really enjoyed the mea...

Walking up and down Frenchman street this place caught our eye. The live music and vibe was great so we decided to eat inside. We got a nice little table by the window and were greeted by our server (I can't remember if she said her name was Joey...or Zoe? Please forgive me lol). She was an absolute doll and perfectly attentive. We ordered the fried chicken livers and two of the ribeye steaks. The livers were really good, and the salads that came with the meal were really good as well. The steaks were cooked to perfection and had that "melt-in-your-mouth" taste. Every bite was mmm worthy. The fingerling potatoes were delicious! Oh and the fried Brussels Sprouts - wow! Do yourself a favor ...

We actually ate here twice during our stay in NOLA. The first time was for dinner but we weren't super hungry, so we both ordered po-boys. He got the oyster po-boy w/ fries and said it was great. No skimping on the oysters and it was dressed just right. I got the shrimp & fried green tomatoes po-boy w/ a salad. Perfect! Actually, for 2 people who weren't that hungry, we mowed through our dinners and got another round of drinks. Mojitos for him & my very first Pimm's Cups which were amazing! What a refreshing hot weather drink! Cucumber in a cocktail sounded weird, but it was spot on! So, on our way back "home" one afternoon, we stopped there for lunch.
